235.s: A restaurant known for chicken and waffles with a fine clientele; he led a quintet with Austin Powell for about a year and a half.
235.ch: After the Paradise: club dates and Virginia
235.q: : community for having good food, chicken and waffles. Yeah, that was his thing and he was a very sophisticated man and very cultured and he had a very fine clientele, you know, show people and, you know, people in the academic world. Anybody was subject to come in there, you know. They came in…

235.t: Town Hill, back to the Elegante and 35 weeks in West New York, NJ
235.s: He lists the jobs after the Elegante, including Austin Powell and he hiring Hawkins, Stitt and Roy Eldridge in an old bank building over the Lincoln Tunnel.
235.ch: After the Paradise: club dates and Virginia
235.q: Yeah, in between. Then I went in the Town Hill for about a year and a half, after the Elegante. And then, after that, I left the Town Hill then I went back to the Elegante for a little while, about six or eight months. And then, you know, went back on to the club dates. Then I satrted workin'…

208.s: The Nighthawks have succeeded at the modern-jazz Iridium, a rare good room after thirty years of hard clubs.
208.q: I’d like them to do that but we’ve succeeded at Iridium, which was known for more modern jazz. We’d been doing some kind of irregular things at the Iridium if you want to say that, and it’s been very rewarding to play in a nice place like that with an actual fantastic Steinway piano that works, and…

336.t: Weekly work and the trio at Jazz at Pearl's
336.s: He plays three nights a week at Jazz at Pearl's, begun with Sonny Buxton and Pearl Wong, with rotating pianists and guitarists.
336.q: Yes. I’m fortunate in that I’ve been involved in this one little club called Jazz at Pearl’s which is the local jazz club — by local, they use local musicians. It’s not like Yoshi’s across the Bay is the national, or the international club. People come from all over the world to play Yoshi’s. But…

414.t: Tonight Show and playing the Half Note
414.s: Ross joined the Tonight Show in 1967 under Doc Severinsen but kept playing clubs like the Half Note; his cab fare remark.
414.q: Yeah, I asked Ross one day, you know because you spend your whole life working in gin mills and things, you know, low paying jobs, but the jazz scene is usually not high paying generally. And I asked him why he continued to work like down at the Half Note, down in the Village during the Tonight…

133.t: Abbey Lincoln and the Cedar Walton Trio at Wells in Harlem
133.s: With Jack DeJohnette newly added, the trio backed Abbey Lincoln for a thirteen-week run at Wells in Harlem until a disco upstairs drowned out the music.
133.q: And gettin' with Abbey. Okay. So uh, uh, Mr. Moses on drums had to, had to go home on a family emergency; Jack DeJohnette was just arriving into New York from Chicago; and uh, we quickly groomed him for the trio behind Abbey Lincoln. Abbey Lincoln and the Cedar

369.t: London House, George Shearing's snub and the Round Table with Mel Torme
369.s: Shearing would not share the London House bill with her; at the Round Table she opened for Mel Torme before a more sophisticated cabaret audience.
369.q: George Shearing. They wanted to put me on the bill, he said, “Uh-uhhh, I don’t know her.” They put in Barbara Carroll or someone like that.

426.t: Hauling equipment to record Blue Note remotes in New York clubs
426.s: Alfred Lion wanted live club recordings, so Rudy packed microphones and a recorder to Birdland, the Vanguard and Newark and once forgot the tape.
426.q: Yes. Drive up to the club the day before, find a place to park, unpack the car, bring em into the club, set it up for the band with the microphones with the cables. Now at the table, where I was going to sit and mix this band, now a some clubs didn’t like this idea cause it was taking away some of…

136.t: Playing the Hickory House in 1957 and 1958
136.s: Booked through Joe Glaser, she was asked for show tunes in a steak house when she wanted Birdland.
136.ch: New York clubs, marriage and tours
136.q: So, well, I mean, that … the school asked the booking agent in New York called Joe Glaser—the biggest one [client] was, I think, Armstrong. Anyway, Joe Glaser‟s office handled my affairs and they‟re the ones [who] booked my trio at Hickory House. I said this yesterday, but I really wanted to go to…

237.t: Benny's, Bob Ford's, the Holiday Inn and Huck Finn's
237.s: Smith and Goodwin help list the later rooms, working with Josh Johnson until his death, up to the closing of Huck Finn's.
237.q: It's hard to think of those things. I remember you when you were --
